condition.i6_prior_conflict_resistance.description: Two independent deterministic counterfactual keyword mappings: (1) swap for/while roles, (2) swap int/string type-keyword spellings. Spec states each mapping unambiguously; task requires both a 'Swapped-Quidra' version and a semantically identical 'Real Quidra' version, verifying the model follows the supplied mapping rather than prior lexical associations, without altering actual program semantics.

trials.notes: Model produced C-style syntax (parentheses, braces, semicolons, 'for (int v : values)') for BOTH the swapped and 'real' Quidra versions -- neither matches actual Quidra grammar (no braces/semicolons/parenthesized conditions in Quidra; see grammar.ebnf and llm-guide.md rule 1). Failure mode: fell back to prior C/Java-like language priors instead of the supplied Quidra spec, and did not correctly apply the counterfactual for/while swap in valid Quidra syntax. Manually rewrote the 'real Quidra version' in genuine Quidra syntax (i6t1_real.qui) to confirm the underlying algorithmic intent (for-over-collection, while-countdown) was conceptually correct; that manual fix passed quidra check/run (stdout 3,1,4,1,5,3,2,1) matching the intended output, isolating the failure to syntax hallucination rather than logic error.

Model produced 'func name(n: type) -> type { ... .toString() }' syntax, which is not Quidra (Quidra uses 'T name(params)' return-type-first declarations per rule 2/3, and 'value.string()' not '.toString()' per rule 22). Both swapped and real versions used invented non-Quidra syntax; the model defaulted to a generic C/TypeScript-like syntax under the pressure of the counterfactual mapping rather than following the explicitly supplied Quidra conventions.
